q: A billionaire moves into a town of 1,000 people. Which average of income changes a lot?
why: The mean adds everyone up, so one huge value pulls it far up. The median only looks at the middle person.

q: The mean is one of the data values.
why: The mean of 1 and 2 is 1.5, which isn't in the data. The average family has 2.4 children, but no family does.

q: If the mean is much bigger than the median, the data are probably skewed to the right.
why: Fact. A long tail of big values pulls the mean up but barely moves the median.

lines: The middle two of 7, 2, 9, 3 are 2 and 9
why: Sort first: 2, 3, 7, 9. The middle two are 3 and 7, so the median is 5.

q: The mean of 5 numbers is 10. Four of them are 8, 9, 11 and 12. What is the fifth?
why: Mean 10 for 5 numbers means a total of 50. 50 − 40 = 10.
